summary: Turn reproductive health evidence into policy briefs, budget analysis and implementation scorecards. Explore the five-day training outline.
lede: Reproductive health policy and advocacy turn evidence about service needs into feasible proposals and trackable policy action. For intermediate policy officers, programme managers and civil society advocates, the training provides practice in mapping policy issues, comparing options for feasibility and equity, reviewing budgets and drafting advocacy briefs. Participants also build implementation scorecards with SMART indicators to track follow-through.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who shape reproductive health policy, make the case for policy change or monitor whether decisions translate into funded action. It suits intermediate-level practitioners with familiarity in reproductive health programmes, public policy or advocacy.
modules: Theory of Change for Policy Action
WHO Building Blocks and Policy Coordination
Policy Briefs and Advocacy Action Plans
prerequisites: Working familiarity with reproductive health programmes, public policy processes or advocacy is expected. No programming is required; exercises use policy scenarios, written templates and spreadsheet-based budget review.
